paragraphs.title: The Song of Victory at the Sea

easy.question: Who sang the song?
answers: Moses and the children of Israel
Pharaoh and his servants
Aaron and the priests
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Then sang Moses and the children of Israel.”

easy.question: To whom did Moses and the Israelites sing?
answers: To Moses
To the Lord
To Pharaoh
easy.explanation: They said, “I will sing unto the Lord,” so the song was directed to Him.

easy.question: What happened to the horse and its rider?
answers: They fled into the wilderness
They remained in Egypt
They were thrown into the sea
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the horse and his rider hath he thrown into the sea.”

medium.question: Why did the Israelites sing to the Lord at the beginning of the song?
answers: Because the Lord saved them and defeated their enemies
Because they wanted to return to Egypt
Because they were looking for a new king
medium.explanation: The song praises the Lord for His greatness and for throwing the horse and rider into the sea.

medium.question: What does the phrase “he hath triumphed gloriously” emphasize?
answers: That the Lord hid from His enemies
That the Lord won a magnificent victory
That the Lord needed help
medium.explanation: The phrase celebrates the Lord’s greatness and His victory over the enemies of Israel.

medium.question: What connection appears between “He is my God” and “my father’s God”?
answers: The people reject the faith of their ancestors
The people speak only about the future
The Lord is both their personal God and the God of their ancestors
medium.explanation: The verse joins a personal relationship with the Lord to the faith handed down by their ancestors.

challenge.question: What does the title “The Lord is a man of war” mean?
answers: A poetic picture of the Lord as a warrior defeating His enemies
That a man named the Lord went to war
A description of one of Israel’s soldiers
challenge.explanation: This poetic description emphasizes that the Lord acts powerfully against Israel’s enemies and gives victory.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the movement from “my strength” to “my salvation”?
answers: That the people relied only on their military strength
That the Lord is both the source of strength and the one who saves
That salvation came by chance
challenge.explanation: The verse presents the Lord as Israel’s strength and as the one who brings salvation.

challenge.question: Which detail most strongly conveys awe at the Lord’s greatness?
answers: The mention of a father
The mention of the sea alone
The declaration that He triumphed gloriously
challenge.explanation: The emphatic wording heightens the description of the Lord’s greatness and victory.

questions.question: What does the title “The Lord is a man of war” mean?
answers: A poetic picture of the Lord as a warrior defeating His enemies
That a man named the Lord went to war
A description of one of Israel’s soldiers
questions.explanation: This poetic description emphasizes that the Lord acts powerfully against Israel’s enemies and gives victory.

questions.question: What can we infer from the movement from “my strength” to “my salvation”?
answers: That the people relied only on their military strength
That the Lord is both the source of strength and the one who saves
That salvation came by chance
questions.explanation: The verse presents the Lord as Israel’s strength and as the one who brings salvation.

questions.question: Which detail most strongly conveys awe at the Lord’s greatness?
answers: The mention of a father
The mention of the sea alone
The declaration that He triumphed gloriously
questions.explanation: The emphatic wording heightens the description of the Lord’s greatness and victory.

easy.question: Who drowned in the sea?
answers: Pharaoh and his army
The Israelites
The shepherds of Midian
easy.explanation: The verse says that Pharaoh’s chariots and army were cast into the Red Sea.

easy.question: What covered the Egyptians?
answers: Clouds
The depths
Sand
easy.explanation: The song says, “The depths have covered them.”

easy.question: What were the enemies compared to when they fell into the water?
answers: Birds
Grass
A stone and lead
easy.explanation: The verses compare them to a stone and to lead sinking in the water.

medium.question: What caused the enemies to be covered by the sea?
answers: The Lord’s wind moved the waters, and the sea covered them
The Israelites threw stones at them
The Egyptians stopped their chariots
medium.explanation: The wind sent by the Lord gathered the waters, and the sea then covered the enemies.

medium.question: In the phrase “the floods stood upright as an heap,” what happened to the waters?
answers: They became a small drop
They stood like a heap or wall
They made a loud noise
medium.explanation: The verse pictures the waters standing together like a heap or wall.

medium.question: What order of events is described in the verses?
answers: The enemy drowned and then began pursuing
The enemy divided the spoil and then returned to Egypt
The enemy planned to pursue and take spoil, and then the Lord’s wind and sea destroyed them
medium.explanation: First the enemy planned to pursue and divide the spoil; afterward the wind and sea overwhelmed them.

challenge.question: What is emphasized by the repeated phrase “Thy right hand, O Lord”?
answers: The Lord’s power and action
The place where Moses stood
The number of enemies
challenge.explanation: The right hand symbolizes power and strength, and the repetition emphasizes the Lord’s defeat of the enemy.

challenge.question: Why is the comparison to lead especially fitting for the enemies?
answers: Because lead floats on water
Because lead is heavy and sinks quickly
Because lead is used to build chariots
challenge.explanation: Lead is heavy, so the comparison emphasizes the enemies’ sinking in the water.

challenge.question: How do the descriptions of the Lord’s breath and wind relate to each other?
answers: Both say that the waters disappeared by themselves
Both say that the enemy blew against Israel
Both describe the Lord’s wind affecting the waters
challenge.explanation: Both expressions describe the Lord’s breath or wind gathering the waters and then causing the sea to cover the enemy.

questions.question: What is emphasized by the repeated phrase “Thy right hand, O Lord”?
answers: The Lord’s power and action
The place where Moses stood
The number of enemies
questions.explanation: The right hand symbolizes power and strength, and the repetition emphasizes the Lord’s defeat of the enemy.

answers: Because lead floats on water

questions.explanation: Lead is heavy, so the comparison emphasizes the enemies’ sinking in the water.

questions.question: How do the descriptions of the Lord’s breath and wind relate to each other?
answers: Both say that the waters disappeared by themselves
Both say that the enemy blew against Israel
Both describe the Lord’s wind affecting the waters
questions.explanation: Both expressions describe the Lord’s breath or wind gathering the waters and then causing the sea to cover the enemy.

paragraphs.title: Who Is Like You Among the Gods?

easy.question: To whom is the question “Who is like unto thee?” addressed?
answers: The Lord
Moses
The Egyptians
easy.explanation: The question is addressed to the Lord: “Who is like unto thee, O Lord?”

easy.question: How is the Lord described in the verse?
answers: Weak and afraid
Glorious in holiness and doing wonders
An ordinary man
easy.explanation: The verse calls the Lord “glorious in holiness” and one who is “doing wonders.”

easy.question: What did the earth do according to verse 12?
answers: It rose up to heaven
It opened before the Israelites
It swallowed the enemies
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the earth swallowed them.”

medium.question: What is the connection between “Who is like unto thee?” and “doing wonders”?
answers: The wonders show that no one is like the Lord
The wonders show that the Lord is weak
The question is unrelated to the description
medium.explanation: The Lord’s wonders support the claim that no one can compare with Him.

medium.question: What is the order of events in verse 12?
answers: The earth swallowed them, and then the Lord stretched out His hand
The Lord stretched out His hand, and then the earth swallowed them
The Lord stopped doing wonders, and then the earth opened
medium.explanation: The verse first describes the Lord stretching out His hand and then the earth swallowing the enemies.

medium.question: In “fearful in praises,” what does “fearful” mean?
answers: Inspiring awe and reverence
Very sad
Small and weak
medium.explanation: In this context, “fearful” describes the Lord as inspiring awe and reverence because of His great deeds.

challenge.question: Why is the question “Who is like unto thee?” repeated?
answers: To show that the Lord forgot His name
To emphasize that no one compares with the Lord
To describe two different gods
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes the Lord’s uniqueness and incomparable greatness.

challenge.question: What is the likely meaning of “Thy right hand” in “Thou stretchedst out thy right hand”?
answers: The Lord’s power and action
Another person’s hand
Only a geographical direction
challenge.explanation: In this context of divine action and judgment, the right hand symbolizes the Lord’s power and activity.

challenge.question: What can we learn from the object “them” in “the earth swallowed them”?
answers: That the earth swallowed one thing
That the earth swallowed a group of people
That the Lord was swallowed by the earth
challenge.explanation: The plural object refers to the enemies as a group whom the earth swallowed.

questions.question: Why is the question “Who is like unto thee?” repeated?
answers: To show that the Lord forgot His name
To emphasize that no one compares with the Lord
To describe two different gods
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes the Lord’s uniqueness and incomparable greatness.

questions.question: What is the likely meaning of “Thy right hand” in “Thou stretchedst out thy right hand”?
answers: The Lord’s power and action
Another person’s hand
Only a geographical direction
questions.explanation: In this context of divine action and judgment, the right hand symbolizes the Lord’s power and activity.

questions.question: What can we learn from the object “them” in “the earth swallowed them”?
answers: That the earth swallowed one thing
That the earth swallowed a group of people
That the Lord was swallowed by the earth
questions.explanation: The plural object refers to the enemies as a group whom the earth swallowed.

paragraphs.title: The Way to the Land and the Sanctuary

easy.question: What did the Lord do for Israel according to verse 13?
answers: He redeemed and led them
He punished them
He scattered them among the nations
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Lord led forth the people whom He had redeemed.

easy.question: Who trembled and feared when they heard about Israel’s departure?
answers: Only the Israelites
The nations and the inhabitants of Palestina
Only the priests
easy.explanation: The verses say that the peoples heard, and sorrow took hold of the inhabitants of Palestina.

easy.question: What is said about the Lord’s reign at the end of the passage?
answers: It will end soon
It belongs only to Israel
The Lord shall reign for ever and ever
easy.explanation: Verse 18 concludes, “The Lord shall reign for ever and ever.”

medium.question: Why were the surrounding peoples afraid according to the passage?
answers: They heard about the Lord’s power and deeds
They could not find their way
The Israelites asked them for help
medium.explanation: The nations heard about Israel’s redemption and the Lord’s power, so fear and trembling seized them.

medium.question: In “sorrow shall take hold on the inhabitants of Palestina,” what does “sorrow” express?
answers: Joy
Fear and trembling
Rest
medium.explanation: Here “sorrow” describes the fear and trembling that seized the inhabitants of Palestina.

medium.question: What is the general order described in the verses?
answers: The sanctuary was built, then redemption came, and finally fear
Fear came first, then slavery, and finally the exodus
Redemption and guidance, the fear of the nations, and then entry into the land and establishment of the sanctuary
medium.explanation: The Lord first redeems and leads His people; the nations then fear; finally Israel is brought into the land and sanctuary.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the repeated words “till thy people pass over” in verse 16?
answers: The journey is described as a passage leading to the promised destination
The people immediately returned to Egypt
The nations passed over instead of Israel
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes Israel’s journey onward until reaching the land and inheritance prepared by the Lord.

challenge.question: What is the connection between “the people which thou hast redeemed” and “the people which thou hast purchased”?
answers: They refer to two different peoples
Both describe Israel as the people whom the Lord rescued and claimed as His own
The first refers to Egypt and the second to Palestina
challenge.explanation: Both statements refer to Israel: the Lord redeemed them from slavery and claimed them as His people.

challenge.question: What change in Israel’s situation is described throughout the passage?
answers: From a wandering people to a destroyed people
From a frightened people to a fleeing people
From a redeemed and guided people to a people planted in their land
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with redemption and guidance and ends with Israel being brought into and planted in its inheritance.

questions.question: What can we understand from the repeated words “till thy people pass over” in verse 16?
answers: The journey is described as a passage leading to the promised destination
The people immediately returned to Egypt
The nations passed over instead of Israel
questions.explanation: The repetition emphasizes Israel’s journey onward until reaching the land and inheritance prepared by the Lord.

questions.question: What is the connection between “the people which thou hast redeemed” and “the people which thou hast purchased”?
answers: They refer to two different peoples
Both describe Israel as the people whom the Lord rescued and claimed as His own
The first refers to Egypt and the second to Palestina
questions.explanation: Both statements refer to Israel: the Lord redeemed them from slavery and claimed them as His people.

answers: From a wandering people to a destroyed people
From a frightened people to a fleeing people
From a redeemed and guided people to a people planted in their land
questions.explanation: The passage begins with redemption and guidance and ends with Israel being brought into and planted in its inheritance.

paragraphs.title: Miriam Leads with Timbrels and Dancing

easy.question: Who took the timbrel in her hand?
answers: Miriam
Pharaoh
Aaron’s sister
easy.explanation: The verse says that Miriam the prophetess took a timbrel in her hand.

easy.question: How did the Israelites travel through the sea?
answers: In ships
On dry land
On horses
easy.explanation: The children of Israel went on dry land in the midst of the sea.

easy.question: What did the women use and do after Miriam?
answers: Trumpets and singing
Harps and running
Timbrels and dancing
easy.explanation: The women went out after Miriam with timbrels and dances.

medium.question: What did Miriam and the women do after Israel was rescued from the Egyptians?
answers: They sang to the Lord and celebrated
They returned to Egypt
They built ships
medium.explanation: After the rescue, Miriam and the women led singing and celebration to the Lord.

medium.question: Why did Miriam say to the women, “Sing ye to the Lord”?
answers: Because they wanted to learn to dance
Because the Lord had triumphed and thrown Pharaoh’s horse and rider into the sea
Because they were looking for Moses
medium.explanation: Miriam connected the song with the Lord’s victory over the Egyptians at the sea.

medium.question: What does the phrase “he hath triumphed gloriously” communicate?
answers: That the Lord fell asleep
That the Lord moved slowly
That the Lord rose up in greatness and won by His power
medium.explanation: In the song, the phrase describes the Lord’s greatness and His victory over the enemy.

challenge.question: What is the main contrast in verse 19 between Pharaoh’s horse and the Israelites?
answers: Pharaoh’s horse went into the sea, while the Israelites went on dry land
Pharaoh’s horse crossed on dry land, while the Israelites drowned
Both crossed the sea in the same way
challenge.explanation: The verse contrasts the Egyptians being overwhelmed by the waters with Israel crossing on dry land.

challenge.question: What does the repetition of “he hath triumphed gloriously” emphasize?
answers: The length of the journey in the wilderness
The Lord’s greatness and the power of His victory
The number of women who followed Miriam
challenge.explanation: The repeated wording reinforces the Lord’s greatness and powerful victory over the Egyptians.

challenge.question: What can we infer from Miriam leading the women with timbrels and dances?
answers: The women remained outside the event
The women were afraid to sing
The women actively joined in thanksgiving and victory celebration
challenge.explanation: Miriam led the women, who took part in singing, music, and dancing as an expression of thanks to the Lord.

questions.question: What is the main contrast in verse 19 between Pharaoh’s horse and the Israelites?
answers: Pharaoh’s horse went into the sea, while the Israelites went on dry land
Pharaoh’s horse crossed on dry land, while the Israelites drowned
Both crossed the sea in the same way
questions.explanation: The verse contrasts the Egyptians being overwhelmed by the waters with Israel crossing on dry land.

questions.question: What does the repetition of “he hath triumphed gloriously” emphasize?
answers: The length of the journey in the wilderness
The Lord’s greatness and the power of His victory
The number of women who followed Miriam
questions.explanation: The repeated wording reinforces the Lord’s greatness and powerful victory over the Egyptians.

questions.question: What can we infer from Miriam leading the women with timbrels and dances?
answers: The women remained outside the event
The women were afraid to sing
The women actively joined in thanksgiving and victory celebration
questions.explanation: Miriam led the women, who took part in singing, music, and dancing as an expression of thanks to the Lord.

easy.question: From where did Moses lead Israel?
answers: The Red Sea
Egypt
Mount Sinai
easy.explanation: The verse says, “So Moses brought Israel from the Red sea.”

easy.question: How many days did the Israelites travel in the wilderness without finding water?
answers: One day
Three days
Seven days
easy.explanation: The verse says they went three days in the wilderness and found no water.

easy.question: What did the people ask Moses?
answers: Where shall we go?
When shall we arrive?
What shall we drink?
easy.explanation: The people asked, “What shall we drink?”

medium.question: Why could the Israelites not drink the water of Marah?
answers: Because the water was bitter
Because the water was deep
Because the water was cold
medium.explanation: The verse explains that they could not drink it because the waters were bitter.

medium.question: What does “the people murmured against Moses” mean?
answers: They thanked Moses
They complained to Moses
They walked behind Moses
medium.explanation: To murmur against Moses means to complain to him, as shown by their question, “What shall we drink?”

medium.question: Why was the place called Marah?
answers: Because Moses named it before they arrived
Because it had no water at all
Because its waters were bitter
medium.explanation: The place was called Marah because its waters were bitter and unfit to drink.

challenge.question: What was the difference between Israel’s situation in the wilderness and at Marah?
answers: In the wilderness they found no water, while at Marah they found water but could not drink it
In the wilderness they drank water, while at Marah they found no place
In the wilderness the water was sweet, while at Marah it was cold
challenge.explanation: In the wilderness they found no water at all; at Marah there was water, but its bitterness prevented them from drinking it.

challenge.question: What can we infer from the people asking, “What shall we drink?”
answers: They had already found fresh water
They were worried because of the lack of drinkable water
They wanted to leave the wilderness immediately
challenge.explanation: The question expresses concern and distress caused by the lack of water suitable for drinking.

challenge.question: What does the statement that the place was therefore called Marah show about the water and its name?
answers: The water arrived after the place was named
The people did not know the source of the name
The place received its name because of the taste of the water
challenge.explanation: The name reflects the cause: because the waters were bitter, the place was called Marah.

questions.question: What was the difference between Israel’s situation in the wilderness and at Marah?
answers: In the wilderness they found no water, while at Marah they found water but could not drink it
In the wilderness they drank water, while at Marah they found no place
In the wilderness the water was sweet, while at Marah it was cold
questions.explanation: In the wilderness they found no water at all; at Marah there was water, but its bitterness prevented them from drinking it.

questions.question: What can we infer from the people asking, “What shall we drink?”
answers: They had already found fresh water
They were worried because of the lack of drinkable water
They wanted to leave the wilderness immediately
questions.explanation: The question expresses concern and distress caused by the lack of water suitable for drinking.

questions.question: What does the statement that the place was therefore called Marah show about the water and its name?
answers: The water arrived after the place was named
The people did not know the source of the name
The place received its name because of the taste of the water
questions.explanation: The name reflects the cause: because the waters were bitter, the place was called Marah.

paragraphs.title: The Sweetening of the Water and the Camp at Elim

easy.question: What happened to the water after the tree was cast into it?
answers: It became sweet
It disappeared
It froze
easy.explanation: The verse says, “the waters were made sweet.”

easy.question: Where did the Israelites arrive in verse 27?
answers: Marah
Elim
Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says, “And they came to Elim.”

easy.question: How many wells of water were at Elim?
answers: Seventy
Ten
Twelve
easy.explanation: The verse says that Elim had twelve wells of water.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events at Marah?
answers: Moses cried to the Lord, the Lord showed him a tree, and the water became sweet
The water became sweet, and then Moses cried to the Lord
The Israelites reached Elim, and then they found the tree
medium.explanation: First Moses cried to the Lord; then the Lord showed him a tree, and the water became sweet after it was cast into the water.

medium.question: What does “there he proved them” mean in context?
answers: He hid them
He tested them
He punished them
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the Lord tested the people’s response and their willingness to listen to Him.

medium.question: According to the passage, what was required for the Lord not to bring the diseases of Egypt upon the people?
answers: That they build a great city
That they remain in the wilderness
That they listen to the Lord and keep His commandments
medium.explanation: The promise is connected with listening to the Lord, doing what is right, and keeping His commandments and statutes.

challenge.question: What can we understand from the fact that the Lord showed Moses a tree instead of simply saying that the water would become sweet?
answers: The Lord gave Moses a practical action that led to the solution
The tree was where the Israelites camped
The water was already sweet before they reached Marah
challenge.explanation: The verse describes a practical instruction: the Lord showed Moses a tree, Moses cast it into the water, and the water became sweet.

challenge.question: What is the possible significance of the exact numbers twelve wells and seventy palm trees at Elim?
answers: The place was very far from Marah
The place provided water and good conditions for camping
The Israelites had to pick all the dates
challenge.explanation: The many wells and palm trees explain why they camped there: it was rich in water and vegetation.

challenge.question: What does “I am the Lord that healeth thee” teach about obedience and the promise?
answers: Healing depends only on the amount of water in the wilderness
The diseases of Egypt would return in any case
The Lord presents Himself as the healer and promises protection when the people obey
challenge.explanation: The verse connects listening to the Lord and keeping His commandments with the promise that the diseases of Egypt would not be placed upon the people.

questions.question: What can we understand from the fact that the Lord showed Moses a tree instead of simply saying that the water would become sweet?
answers: The Lord gave Moses a practical action that led to the solution

questions.explanation: The verse describes a practical instruction: the Lord showed Moses a tree, Moses cast it into the water, and the water became sweet.

questions.explanation: The verse connects listening to the Lord and keeping His commandments with the promise that the diseases of Egypt would not be placed upon the people.
